sections.html:
Aurora spreads across Arapahoe, Adams and Douglas counties, so the office that bills your property tax depends on the address. The city counted 386,261 residents in 2020 (336,035 in Arapahoe County, 47,720 in Adams County and 2,506 in Douglas County), and the 2025 estimate is 410,053. Most of Aurora is in Arapahoe County.

Much of the housing dates from the 1970s and later, after a burst of growth in the late 1970s and early 1980s. Several school districts serve the city: Aurora Public Schools (Adams-Arapahoe 28J) is the main one, and Cherry Creek Public Schools, Bennett 29-J, School District 27J and Douglas County RE-1 cover other parts. The district on your tax bill and the one in a buyer's school search both follow the exact address.

The bill comes from Arapahoe, Adams or Douglas County, depending on the parcel. The Arapahoe County Treasurer handles the largest share of Aurora homes and can be reached at 303-795-4550.

  • 2025 was a revaluation year, and the Arapahoe County Treasurer noted that a temporary state exemption used in 2023 and 2024 had expired.
  • Arapahoe offers a senior and military deferral, with applications accepted January 1 through April 1.
  • The Treasurer takes requests for a Certificate of Taxes Due, which title uses at closing.
  • For 2026, residential rates are 6.8% for local governments and 7.05% for schools.

If your house is in Adams or Douglas County, the same kinds of bills and certificates come from that county's offices, so confirm which one holds your parcel before you call.

sections.h2: What the Arapahoe County Treasurer offers sellers
sections.html:
The Treasurer's tools cover most of what a sale needs.

Treasurer serviceWhat it handles
Certificate of Taxes DueRequests from individuals and title companies, used at closing
Address change requestUpdates your tax mailing address
Tax Search pageView or pay taxes, statements and receipts
Delinquent tax publications and lien sale informationNotices and sale details for unpaid taxes
DeferralSeniors and military, January 1 through April 1

The office also covers a manufactured home buying and selling process. Excess foreclosure funds are now handled by the Public Trustee, not the Treasurer. Owners can opt out of paper statements with the Go Paperless form, and email alerts go out when a statement is posted online. Phone 303-795-4550.

Older owners who plan to sell should ask whether any deferred tax has to be repaid at closing.

Aurora has long run an apartment inspection program. The city council has discussed a registration and licensing program that would cover multifamily and single family rentals, with yearly registration and a local contact for each rental. Any such program would need council approval, and staff would study cost and fees first.

If you own a rental here, check the city's current rules before you list, since registration status can affect a sale.

Arapahoe County had 655,070 residents in 2020, and Littleton is the county seat. Aurora is its largest city. Cities in the county include Centennial, Englewood, Greenwood Village and Cherry Hills Village, so a buyer comparing homes may be weighing several tax districts at once. Adams and Douglas county addresses follow their own offices, and your bill and closing paperwork come from the one that matches your parcel.

Start with the county name and the account number, then look at the school district line, since it ties back to the levy on your parcel. Arapahoe County's Tax Search page lets you view or pay taxes and print statements and receipts. If your statement has gone astray, the address change request on the Treasurer's site fixes the mailing address for future bills.

Because 2025 was a revaluation year and a temporary state exemption used in 2023 and 2024 had expired, a bill may look different from the year before. Call 303-795-4550 if a line on the statement does not make sense. Keep the statement and your payment receipts together, because a title company may ask for both when it checks that earlier years were paid.

sections.h2: Papers to collect before a sale
sections.html:
• The latest tax statement, with the county shown at the top.
  • Any deferral paperwork, if you applied as a senior or a member of the military.
  • Rental registration or inspection records, if the home was a rental.
  • Loan payoff information from your lender.
  • A recent insurance statement, since hail and wind history comes up.

Handing the title company this folder up front cuts the back and forth. Most delays in a closing come from one missing figure, and the tax certificate is often that figure.

Listing on the open market usually means cleaning, repairs, showings and a wait while a buyer's lender completes an appraisal. A cash sale as is skips all of that. It does not skip the title work, so the tax certificate is still ordered, any balance is still paid from your proceeds, and the deed is still recorded.

That makes cash a fit for a house with tenants, a probate timeline or a relocation date you cannot move.

Sellers who used the senior and military deferral should ask the Treasurer what has to be repaid at closing before they accept any offer. Sellers with a rental should check the city's current registration rules at the same time. Knowing both answers early lets you compare a cash offer against a listing on real numbers, and lets the title company plan the closing without surprises. Ask each office to confirm anything important in writing, and keep those papers with your closing file.

sections.h2: What to expect when you sell
sections.html:
A sale here follows the same path whichever county you are in.

  1. Confirm the county that holds your parcel from your tax statement.
  2. Ask the title company to order the Certificate of Taxes Due.
  3. Pay any unpaid tax out of your proceeds at closing.
  4. If you used a deferral, ask what has to be repaid.
  5. Update your tax mailing address with the county afterward.

Buyers' inspectors usually look at the roof and windows first. Tornado warnings are common between April and July, though the tornadoes are usually weak, so storm damage history is worth gathering before you list.

You can list it, sell by owner, or take a cash offer. Cash works well when the house needs repairs, has tenants, or sits in a probate or relocation timeline.

We buy as is. Send your Aurora address and we will tell you how a sale would work, including the tax figures that title will ask for. Because Aurora is large and spread out, comparable sales a few miles apart can differ, so a look at your own block is more useful than a citywide figure.

faqs.q: How many people live in Aurora?
faqs.a: The 2025 estimate is 410,053, and the 2020 census counted 386,261.

faqs.q: Which county do I pay property tax to in Aurora?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Aurora lies in Arapahoe, Adams and Douglas counties, and most residents are in Arapahoe County. Your tax statement shows which one applies.

faqs.q: Does Aurora have a rental license?
faqs.a: The city council has discussed a registration and licensing program for rentals, which would need council approval. Check with the city for the current status.

faqs.q: Is there a tax deferral for older Aurora homeowners?
faqs.a: Arapahoe County lists a senior and military deferral, with applications accepted January 1 through April 1. Ask the Treasurer at 303-795-4550 whether any deferred tax is due at closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Aurora house as is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash sale lets you skip repairs, and any unpaid tax is paid from proceeds at closing.
